entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: 1Ch 14:1, 2 . Hiram's Kindness to David; David's Felicity.

entries.heading: 2. his kingdom was lifted up on high, because of his people Israel
entries.text: 2. his kingdom was lifted up on high, because of his people Israel --This is an important truth, that sovereigns are invested with royal honor and authority, not for their own sakes so much as for that of their people. But while it is true of all kings, it was especially applicable to the monarchs of Israel, and even David was made to know that all his glory and greatness were given only to fit him, as the minister of God, to execute the divine purposes towards the chosen people.

entries.heading: 11. they came up to Baal-perazim; and David smote them there
entries.text: 11. they came up to Baal-perazim; and David smote them there --In an engagement fought at Mount Perazim ( Isa 28:21 ), in the valley of Rephaim, a few miles west of Jerusalem, the Philistines were defeated and put to flight.

entries.heading: 12. when they had left their gods
entries.text: 12. when they had left their gods --(See on 2Sa 5:21 ).

entries.heading: 13. the Philistines yet again spread themselves
entries.text: 13. the Philistines yet again spread themselves --They renewed the campaign the next season, taking the same route. David, according to divine directions, did not confront them.

entries.heading: 14. Go not up after them
entries.text: 14. Go not up after them --The text in 2Sa 5:23 , more correctly has, "Go not up." turn away from them --that is, by stealing round a baca-grove, come upon their rear.

entries.heading: 15. for God is gone forth before thee
entries.text: 15. for God is gone forth before thee --"a sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees," that is, the rustling of the leaves by a strong breeze suddenly rising, was the sign by which David was divinely apprised of the precise moment for the attack. The impetuosity of his onset was like the gush of a pent-up torrent, which sweeps away all in its course; and in allusion to this incident the place got its name.

entries.heading: 16. from Gibeon . . . to Gazer
entries.text: 16. from Gibeon . . . to Gazer --Geba or Gibea ( 2Sa 5:25 ), now Yefa, in the province of Judah. The line from this to Gazer was intersected by the roads which led from Judah to the cities of the Philistines. To recover possession of it, therefore, as was effected by this decisive battle, was equivalent to setting free the whole mountain region of Judah as far as their most westerly slope [Bertheau].
